description: A PNG and an SVG background at device pixel ratio 2: css pixels scale, vectors stay sharp.

florui.css: .box { width: 100px; height: 60px; background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='24' height='24'><rect width='24' height='24' fill='%23f4e9d8'/><circle cx='12' cy='12' r='8' fill='%23c1440e'/><rect x='10' y='2' width='4' height='8' fill='%231b1b2f'/></svg>"), url("data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAwAAAAMCAYAAABWdVznAAAAUUlEQVR4nGP4////gmdRAf9hWMOmAgUjy4EwA4hA1kSUBmRNRGuAaSKoAV0BIT9haCDkJ6wa8PkJpwZcfmJA9xQhPxHUgO4nojQgayJaA0wTALpXUCi3BUCiAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC"); background-size: 24px 24px, 12px 12px; background-repeat: no-repeat, repeat; background-position: 4px 4px, 0 0; }

classification.reason: At device pixel ratio 2 the SVG is drawn by a different rasterizer from Chromium's, so its anti-aliased edge pixels differ, by up to 66 levels in 2.2% of the pixels; the PNG tiles match. Geometry an exact match. Measured against desktop Chrome.
